africa-precipitation-monthly-seasonal.title: Monthly and Seasonal Precipitation from CHIRPS v3 (Africa)
africa-precipitation-monthly-seasonal.summary: Total precipitation (PTOT) aggregated from CHIRPS v3.0 and delivered as per-pixel monthly Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs and per-year rolling 3-month (seasonal) sums over Africa, 1981 to present. This is the rainfall backbone of the KE-ENSO Explorer's seasonal/ENSO analysis: the twelve seasonal windows (JFM, FMA, ..., DJF) are the tri-month sums the notebook compares against ENSO phase and against the drought (SPEI), vegetation (NDVI) and flood layers. A derived aggregation product, not a redistribution of the CHIRPS daily archive.

caveats: Source CHIRPS is public domain ("no restrictions on use"); these reprocessed COGs are released CC-BY-4.0 with attribution to the Climate Hazards Center, UC Santa Barbara. Seasonal windows are labelled by the calendar year in which the window ends (DJF_2020 = Dec 2019 to Feb 2020). Edge windows that the record cannot cover in full are absent (NDJ and DJF 1981; windows ending after the latest monthly file), so not every season x year combination of the template exists.

Rainfall driver for interpreting the drought (SPEI), vegetation (NDVI) and flood layers.

kenya-population-knbs-census.title: KNBS 2019 Census Population Counts by County and Sub-county (Kenya)
kenya-population-knbs-census.summary: Enumerated population from the 2019 Kenya Population and Housing Census (KNBS), as admin-level tables: national, the 47 counties keyed on IEBC COD-AB adm1_pcode, the 345 KNBS sub-county rows in the Bureau's own sub-county universe, and a county x 5-year age group x sex table. The official denominator for anything the KE-ENSO Explorer presents to a Kenyan audience: the census total is 47,564,296, where the two gridded surfaces the Explorer also carries (kenya-population-worldpop 55.2 M, kenya-population-grid3 55.9 M) sit about 17 per cent higher.

licence.attribution: Kenya National Bureau of Statistics (KNBS) Official Statistics

producer.name: Peter Steward
producer.organization: Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT
Kenya National Bureau of Statistics (KNBS)

citation.text: Kenya National Bureau of Statistics (2019). 2019 Kenya Population and Housing Census: Population, Households and Density by Sub-county

caveats:
LICENCE EVIDENCE. Evidence for the licence, recorded because knbs.or.ke itself carries no terms page (the terms-and-conditions URL 404s and the footer asserts "All Rights Reserved"), which is misleading: (1) KNBS operates an Open License Agreement covering its Open Data Platform, granting a worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive licence to use, copy, modify, publish, adapt, distribute and create derivative works for commercial and non-commercial purposes, subject to attribution. (2) KNBS's own account on the Humanitarian Data Exchange published the SAME sub-county table used here - "Distribution of Population by Sex, Number of Households, Land Area, Population Density and Sub County" - under Public Domain / No restrictions (https://data.humdata.org/dataset/kenya-population-per-county-from-census-report-2019). (3) The same census figures are redistributed by UNFPA under CC-BY-3.0-IGO (HDX cod-ps-ken). Required attribution, carried by any product derived from this record: "This product was adapted from the Statistical Office of Kenya's information, which is licensed under the KNBS Open License Agreement."
ADMIN LEVELS DIFFER BY LEVEL. County joins one-for-one with IEBC COD-AB (47 units, adm1_pcode). Sub-county does NOT: COD-AB adm2 is 290 IEBC constituencies while the census reports 345 KNBS sub-county rows (a different universe - constituency splits such as Embakasi East/West/Central against sub-county Embakasi, plus 12 forest and national-park units such as Aberdare Forest and Mt Elgon Forest). Normalised in-county name matching resolves 183 of the 290 COD-AB units, so the adm2 table is published in the KNBS universe, name-keyed, with adm2_pcode_codab filled only where a name matches exactly one COD-AB unit inside the same county and codab_match recording how each row resolved. Use county totals plus a gridded within-county share for any adm2 denominator; do not join this table to COD-AB sub-counties on name. Male + Female (47,562,772) falls 1,524 short of the published Total because KNBS suppresses the intersex count below national level; the residual is carried as pop_intersex. The age-and-sex table comes from HDX cod-ps-ken (UNFPA, CC-BY-3.0-IGO), which redistributes the same census (Volume III) with adm1 p-codes attached. DO NOT SWITCH THE SOURCE TO THE HDX COPY of the sub-county table, despite its cleaner licence status: that copy is defective. It carries 346 rows to this source's 345 because the Tharaka-Nithi COUNTY total (393,177) appears as if it were a sub-county, inflating the national figure to 47,957,473 against the published 47,564,296. This ingest uses the knbs.or.ke workbook, which reconciles exactly. (It also spells Kutulo as "Kotulo"; same value, harmless.)

avoid.reason: The two sub-county universes differ; only 183 of 290 COD-AB units have an exact in-county name match.

enso-driver-dmi.title: Indian Ocean Dipole Mode Index (DMI, NOAA CPC / ERSSTv6)
enso-driver-dmi.summary: Monthly Dipole Mode Index for the Indian Ocean as published by the NOAA Climate Prediction Center: the sea-surface-temperature anomaly of the western tropical Indian Ocean (50E-70E, 10S-10N) minus that of the south-eastern tropical Indian Ocean (90E-110E, 10S-0), computed from ERSSTv6 against a 1991-2020 climatology. A federated record - the Adaptation Atlas cites this index but does not host or redistribute it.

licence.attribution: NOAA Climate Prediction Center / Physical Sciences Laboratory

producer.organization: NOAA Climate Prediction Center

producer.name: Peter Steward
producer.organization: Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT

citation.text: NOAA Climate Prediction Center (2026). Indian Ocean Dipole Mode Index (DMI), monthly, ERSSTv6, 1991-2020 climatology

caveats: SOURCE CHOICE IS DELIBERATE. The widely cited DMI series served by NOAA PSL is computed from HadISST, which is Crown Copyright, Met Office, released under the UK Non-Commercial Government Licence - downloads permitted for private study and scientific research, any other use requiring a licence from the Met Office IPR officer. That is incompatible with the open licences Adaptation Atlas products carry, so this record uses the CPC ERSSTv6 series instead, which is a work of the US Government with no constraints on access or use. The swap is not only a licensing fix. CPC computes RONI (record enso-driver-roni) from the same ERSSTv6 reconstruction against the same 1991-2020 base period, so pairing CPC DMI with CPC RONI puts both drivers on one SST basis and one climatology. Pairing HadISST DMI with ERSSTv6 RONI does not, and mixing reconstructions is the same class of error as mixing RONI with the raw Nino 3.4 anomaly. VALUES DIFFER FROM THE HadISST SERIES. A different SST reconstruction and a different climatology produce a different series, not a relabelled one. Any analysis that selected analogue seasons from the HadISST-based DMI must be re-run after switching; do not splice the two. COVERAGE. Monthly, 1950-01 onward, updated automatically on the first Thursday of each month; the live file ran to 2026-08 when this record was written. This also resolves the staleness in the KE-ENSO staging, where DMI was NULL for all of 2025 in both seasons - a gap that made 2025 unusable as an analogue year and that failed SILENTLY in a z-scored analogue distance. The file carries both poles (WTIO, SETIO) alongside the index, so the two legs of a dipole event can be distinguished rather than inferred from the difference alone.

avoid.use: Splicing this series onto the HadISST-based DMI served by NOAA PSL.
avoid.reason: Different SST reconstruction and different climatology, so the join introduces a step change that would be read as a physical signal.
avoid.use_instead: One source end to end; this one, which is also the openly licensed option.

avoid.use: Weighting IOD and ENSO equally in an unscaled analogue distance.
avoid.reason: For Kenya OND the two axes have very different spread (ENSO sd about 1.179 against IOD about 0.362), so an unscaled squared distance lets ENSO dominate by roughly ten to one - backwards for the season IOD matters most in.
avoid.use_instead: Z-score each driver axis before computing distance.

intended_uses: Characterising Indian Ocean Dipole state when selecting analogue seasons for Kenyan seasonal outlooks.
Pairing with RONI (record enso-driver-roni) on a single SST reconstruction and base period.

kenya-flood-exposure-intersect.title: Kenya Flood x Exposure, Per-Sub-County Tables
kenya-flood-exposure-intersect.summary: Pre-computed flood x exposure statistics for Kenya's 290 IEBC sub-counties (admin 2), as three small Parquet tables the KE-ENSO Explorer reads directly (DuckDB-WASM) instead of intersecting heavy rasters and vectors in the browser. Two hazard products - Copernicus GFM observed flood (per season x year, 2018 to 2025) and JRC modelled return-period flood hazard - are each crossed with population (WorldPop constrained 100 m grid, levelled to the official KNBS county totals), classified roads and the electricity transmission grid (length exposed) and health and school facilities (count exposed); a third table holds the per-sub-county denominators. Tables carry no geometry: join on adm2_pcode to the boundary record kenya-admin-codab.

producer.name: Peter Steward
producer.organization: Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT

citation.text: Steward, P. (2026). Kenya flood x exposure per-sub-county tables, Africa Agriculture Adaptation Atlas (KE-ENSO Explorer)

caveats:
Derived aggregate statistics; no input geometry is redistributed. Please attribute the inputs: Copernicus GFM and JRC Global Flood Maps (Copernicus / European Commission), WorldPop constrained population (CC-BY-4.0), OpenStreetMap roads and HOTOSM facilities ((c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL), KPLC grid (CC0-1.0, energydata.info), IEBC COD-AB boundaries (OCHA, CC-BY-3.0-IGO). In the GFM table, observed_pct is the SAR-observed share of the sub-county in that season: low values mean sparse observation, not absence of flooding. Road and grid kilometres are cell-resolution approximations (in-cell line length within flooded cells). Every table also carries adm1_pcode, adm1_name and adm2_name label columns. POPULATION METHOD (issue #28), stated in full. Headcounts are NOT raw gridded pixel sums. Every published sub-county population is built as three explicit factors, each published as its own column:
  pop_adm2 = pop_adm2_grid x pop_scale_census x pop_growth_county
(1) pop_adm2_grid - the 100 m gridded pixel sum, which supplies the SHARE of the county's people
    living in that sub-county, and nothing else.
(2) pop_scale_census = census county total / gridded county total - replaces the LEVEL of the
    gridded surface with the enumerated KNBS 2019 census, county by county. The gridded surfaces
    run about 17 per cent above the census (WorldPop constrained ~55.2 M, GRID3 ~55.9 M, census
    47,564,296), so this factor is ~0.855 nationally but spans 0.324-1.394 across individual
    counties (measured on the published grid, 2026-09-17): WorldPop exceeds the census by up to
    threefold in some counties and falls below it in others. Any aggregate therefore moves by a
    weighted mix of county factors, not by the national one - flood-exposed population sits mostly
    in low-factor counties, so the GFM exposed total fell about 35 per cent where the national
    denominator fell 14 per cent. No time component.
(3) pop_growth_county = target county total / census county total - the county's proportional
    CHANGE OVER TIME, from the KNBS Vol XVI projections (record
    kenya-population-knbs-projections). Exactly 1.0 when the denominator is the census itself.
County is the only level where any of this is defensible: COD-AB adm2 is 290 IEBC constituencies while the census reports 345 KNBS sub-counties, and only 183 names match (record kenya-population-knbs-census); KNBS does not project below county at all. FIXED-SHARE ASSUMPTION. Each sub-county's share of its county is held constant at the gridded 2020 distribution, so every sub-county in a county moves by exactly that county's percentage change. Sub-county-specific growth is NOT represented: a fast-urbanising sub-county and a depopulating one in the same county grow at the same rate here. Growth does vary between counties - the 2025 factors span 1.03 to 1.15 - but not within one. YEAR MATCHING (the published default from 2026-09-17). The GFM table records OBSERVED floods and carries a year, so a single fixed denominator is wrong in one direction or the other: the 2019 census undercounts a 2024 flood by roughly 9 per cent, and a 2025 projection overcounts a 2018 one by a similar margin. Each GFM row is therefore levelled against ITS OWN year's county population, and pop_year records which year was used. Years the KNBS projections cover (2020 onward) use them; 2018 and 2019 fall back to the enumerated census, because nothing official projects backwards from the 2020 base and inventing a figure would be worse than stating the fallback. Consequence for consumers: pop_source VARIES BY ROW in the GFM table - "knbs-census-2019" for 2018-2019 and "knbs-projection-<year>" thereafter - so do not read one value and assume it applies to the file. The JRC table is a return-period hazard with no event year, and the totals table is a static denominator, so both take a single stated reference year (pop_year, same on every row). TWO DEFINITIONS OF THE GROWTH FACTOR, recorded in pop_method:
  county-growth-from-<base year> - pop_growth_county = projection(year) / projection(base year,
    2020). The enumerated census remains the level and KNBS supplies only the shape of change;
    national 2025 lands near 51.96 M because the ~2.6 per cent step KNBS puts between census night
    (August 2019) and its own 2020 base is deliberately not imported.
  county-level - pop_growth_county = projection(year) / census(2019), so the county total IS the
    published official projection and national 2025 is 53,330,978 - the figure a Kenyan
    counterpart would quote - at the cost of superseding the census anchor with the KNBS base-level
    revision.

processing.description: Zonal intersect of the flood masks with the sub-county polygons, the population raster, rasterised per-cell road and grid line length, and facility points. kenya-population-knbs-projections.title: KNBS Official Population Projections by County, 2020-2045 (Kenya)
kenya-population-knbs-projections.summary: Kenya's official cohort-component population projections, from the 2019 KPHC Analytical Report on Population Projections (Volume XVI, KNBS 2022), tabulated from the report's Appendix 5 as county x year x 5-year age group x sex, keyed on IEBC COD-AB adm1_pcode. licence.attribution: Kenya National Bureau of Statistics (KNBS) Official Statistics

producer.name: Peter Steward
producer.organization: Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT
Kenya National Bureau of Statistics (KNBS)

citation.text: Kenya National Bureau of Statistics (2022). 2019 Kenya Population and Housing Census, Analytical Report on Population Projections (Volume XVI)

caveats:
LICENCE EVIDENCE. Weaker footing than the census record, and the difference is worth stating. KNBS's Open License Agreement grants worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive rights to reuse, adapt, redistribute and create derivative works with attribution - but it is scoped to data published on the KNBS Open Data Platform, and Volume XVI is a PDF hosted on knbs.or.ke. Unlike the 2019 census tables, no licensed mirror of these projections exists anywhere (searched HDX, open.africa and the Kenya data portal, 2026-09-17): UNFPA's COD-PS covers the census, not Volume XVI. What is published here is a derived tabulation of figures printed in a public national statistical report, attributed, not a copy of the report. Confirm with KNBS before this record is contributed to cdh-catalog. Required attribution: "This product was adapted from the Statistical Office of Kenya's information, which is licensed under the KNBS Open License Agreement."
COUNTY ONLY. Volume XVI does not project below county - no sub-county name appears anywhere in the report - so this record stops at county. The KE-ENSO exposure tables (record kenya-flood-exposure-intersect) do carry sub-county figures for a projection year, and the way they get there is stated there in full: each sub-county's share of its county is held fixed at the gridded 2020 distribution and the whole county is moved by its own percentage change from this table (pop_growth_county), with the enumerated census supplying the level. That means no sub-county-specific growth is represented; growth varies between counties (2025 factors span 1.03 to 1.15) but is uniform within one. Anyone wanting genuine sub-county differentials needs a source that produces them - this one does not. YEAR COVERAGE IS UNEVEN. The report's annual panels cover 2020-2035; 2040 and 2045 appear only in the five-yearly milestone panel, so 2036-2039 and 2041-2044 are absent. TWO SOURCE DEFECTS, both handled and logged by the ingest rather than silently absorbed. (1) Busia 2030, age 80+, female reads 3,120 in the 2030-2035 panel against 5,799 in the two other panels that carry 2030; the printed row total (9,714) reconciles only with 5,799, so 5,799 is used. (2) Kiambu's 2026-2030 panel labels its open-ended top age group "80-84" where every other panel says "80+"; it is relabelled "80+", without which it would double-count against the overlapping panels. KNBS rounds each printed cell independently, so sums do not close exactly: age groups land within five people of the printed All Ages row, and the 47 counties sum to roughly 15 to 20 people below the national row in every year. The identical report is also hosted as ...-Analytical-Report-on-Population-Projections-Vol-XVI.pdf (2024/05, 32.9 MB); its extracted text is identical to the 2023/09 upload used here.

kenya-flood-gfm.title: Kenya Observed Flood Extent (Copernicus GFM, Sentinel-1)
kenya-flood-gfm.summary: Observed flood extent for Kenya from the Copernicus Emergency Management Service Global Flood Monitoring (GFM) product, which classifies flooding from every Sentinel-1 SAR acquisition (ensemble of the DLR, TU Wien and LIST algorithms; permanent and reference water excluded). Delivered as ~111 m aggregates built directly from the 20 m SAR tiles: a monthly flood-occurrence layer with its valid-observation count, a rolling 3-month (seasonal) layer aligned to the KE-ENSO Explorer precipitation seasons, and a full-record history (occurrence frequency and ever-flooded footprint), 2018 to present. Replaces the MODIS Global Flood Database (ended 2018) with a cloud-penetrating, continuously updated SAR record. The 20 m per-acquisition archive is not materialised here (16,000+ acquisitions); it can be re-pulled from the EODC STAC on demand.

caveats: Attribution required: "Contains modified Copernicus Emergency Management Service information [year]". Pixel coding of the flooded layers: 0 = not flooded, 1 = flooded, 255 = not observed (SAR gap or excluded) - 255 is absence of observation, NOT dry; the nobs layer gives the count of valid observations so no-flood is distinguishable from no-observation. Seasonal windows are named by the initials of their months and labelled by the year of their FIRST month (DJF_2018 = Dec 2018 to Feb 2019), so NDJ and DJF exist for 2018 to 2024 only. This differs from the CHIRPS seasonal record (africa-precipitation-monthly-seasonal), which labels NDJ and DJF by the year the window ends; align on those two windows with care. A ~7-year record measures recent observed flood occurrence, not return-period magnitude.
